newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam crude output growth to slow in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam crude output growth to slow in 1997.

text.p: State oil firm Petrovietnam said on Wednesday that Vietnam's crude oil output was expected to reach nine million tonnes in 1997, up slightly more than two percent from last year.
An official said by phone that 1.2 million tonnes was pumped during the first 45 days of this year.
He was unable to provide figures for the same period last year but said the amount represented an increase.

Data from the General Statistics Office (GSO) showed the projected rate of output growth was sharply down from last year when 8.805 million tonnes of crude was pumped, representing an increase of 15.6 percent from 1995.
A GSO report issued last year said Vietnam's oilfields were pumping at close to capacity.
Most of Vietnam's oil comes from offshore fields to the east and south of Ho Chi Minh City.

The country has no refinery and negotiations with foreign firms for a $1.4 billion plant in a remote central coast site chosen by the government have hit difficulties over demands by the firms for better incentives.
The companies involved are Taiwan's Chinese Petroleum Corp, South Korea's LG Group, Stone & Webster, Malaysia's Petronas and U.S.-based Conoco.

Petrovietnam has said it is prepared to go it alone if no agreement is reached. State daily newspapers said on Wednesday that Petrovietnam had been given until March 31 to submit a feasibility study for a solo plan.
